# A scenario listed here must still differ from its ish golden. Each entry
# names the code that owns the remaining difference.

# interactive/app.rs is owned by another lane. `command` is an epsh builtin in
# ish; xshi resolves it as an external program and reports "command: not found".
approved_builtin_classes_remain_available
builtin_lookup_completion_and_explicit_paths_share_the_policy

# interactive/app.rs is owned by another lane: a builtin name that appears only
# after parameter expansion runs as an external lookup instead of ish's
# execution-policy refusal (status 2).
expanded_targets_obey_ish_execution_policy

# interactive/app.rs is owned by another lane: it tries implicit cd before the
# PATH lookup, so a directory named like a PATH binary changes directory.
path_binary_wins_over_implicit_cd

# The shell lexer (interactive/shell/) is outside this lane: `0<&-` parses as a
# background operator instead of closing standard input.
closed_input_redirection_keeps_terminal_ownership

# interactive/z.rs is outside this lane: z does not match a directory whose
# history was recorded through a quoted path.
interactive_final_z_matches_quoted_directory_history

# interactive/app.rs is owned by another lane: resolve_cd_for_history writes an
# absolute cd target without quoting it, so a directory with a space is split.
interactive_final_history_replay_restores_the_recorded_directory

# interactive/app.rs is owned by another lane: command substitution refuses
# non-UTF-8 output, so the raw-byte identity cannot reach the prompt.
prompt_identity_displays_unicode_and_replaces_only_invalid_display_bytes

# The fdu builtin has no reader hand-off path: xshi's line reader drops bytes
# read past Enter.
fdu_rapid_input_handoff_burst
